youtube.title: Earth Had Nuclear Reactors Before Humans
youtube.description:
Earth had natural nuclear reactors roughly two billion years ago. Nobody built them.

At Oklo, in what is now Gabon, uranium-rich rock and groundwater sustained nuclear fission. In 1972, an unexpected uranium-235 abundance helped reveal what had happened.

How could geology create the conditions for a nuclear chain reaction? These reaction zones produced heat, not electricity. Starts and stops inferred from one studied zone are a reconstruction, not a directly observed ancient schedule.

Sources:
Davis, Gould & Sharapov — Oklo review: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.4948
Bentridi et al. — criticality modeling: https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/geoscience/articles/10.1016/j.crte.2011.09.008/
Alex P. Meshik — investigator account: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/ancient-nuclear-reactor/

Original illustrations and AI-generated narration.

#Oklo #NuclearPhysics #Geology
youtube.firstComment: Radioactive rock alone wasn't enough. Water helped slow neutrons, and enough had to trigger another split to sustain the chain. The starts-and-stops reconstruction comes from isotope evidence in one studied zone.
